feature1.prompt: The objective is to reduce redundant AddIndex and RemoveIndex migration operations by optimizing the migration process. This feature focuses on modifying the migration operations so that when an AddIndex operation is immediately countered by a corresponding RemoveIndex operation, the redundant pair is eliminated. The implementation should adjust the internal behavior of migration operations to automatically skip over these canceling actions, resulting in a cleaner migration plan. Expected behavior is that migrations execute without processing unnecessary index modifications, thereby improving efficiency.
feature1.hint_texts: Implement the new 'reduce' method within the IndexOperation class to detect when a RemoveIndex operation matches an existing AddIndex operation and to eliminate both from the migration sequence. Ensure that for operations which do not meet this criterion, the method delegates back to the parent class implementation. The code changes should be confined to django/db/migrations/operations/models.py without affecting the behavior of other migration operations.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py; locate the IndexOperation class and add/modify the reduce method (starting around line 861) to incorporate the optimization logic.

feature2.prompt: The goal is to reduce redundant AddIndex and RemoveIndex migration operations and to verify that such eliminations occur as intended. This feature is aimed at validating that the migration process correctly identifies and omits unnecessary index alterations. The implementation must confirm that when an AddIndex operation is immediately followed by a matching RemoveIndex operation, the redundant operations do not take effect. Expected behavior is that the migration optimization leads to a streamlined sequence of operations, resulting in more efficient migrations.
feature2.hint_texts: Develop a dedicated test case that simulates the scenario where an AddIndex operation is directly canceled by a corresponding RemoveIndex operation. The test should assert that the resulting migration operations list does not include the redundant pair. Use the provided diff as guidance to add a new test method that confirms the optimization logic implemented in feature1.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/migrations/test_optimizer.py; add a new test method named test_add_remove_index that exercises the migration reduction by invoking the optimization logic of the reduce method.

tests.PASS_TO_PASS: None - this feature focuses on the new test validating the reduction logic.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features work with the migration operation logic; feature1 modifies the core implementation in django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, while feature2 creates a test in tests/migrations/test_optimizer.py to validate that implementation.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 provides the optimized 'reduce' method which must be exercised by the new test in feature2. The integration of these features should occur through continuous integration runs to ensure that the optimized migration operations yield the expected behavior without regressing existing functionalities.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers for feature1 and feature2 need to coordinate on the precise behavior of the reduce method. Regular discussions should verify that the new test case in feature2 accurately reflects the intended optimization and that any modifications in feature1 are promptly communicated to the tester.
